questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable energy resource?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a fossil fuel and a non-renewable resource -- it will eventually run out and cannot be replenished within a human lifetime.

questions.stem: What does 'renewable' mean when describing an energy resource?

options.text: It produces no energy at all
It will not run out and is naturally replenished
It can only be used once

questions.explanation: A renewable energy resource is one that will not run out because it is naturally replenished, such as wind, solar, and tidal energy.

questions.stem: Which three resources are classified as fossil fuels?
questions.explanation: The three fossil fuels are coal, oil (petroleum), and natural gas. They were formed from the remains of organisms over millions of years.

questions.stem: What is the main environmental concern with burning fossil fuels?

options.text: They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (CO2), a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming and climate change.

questions.stem: Which renewable energy source depends on the gravitational pull of the Moon?
questions.explanation: Tidal energy is driven by the gravitational pull of the Moon (and to a lesser extent the Sun), which causes the rise and fall of tides.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of wind energy is that:

options.text: It is unreliable because wind does not blow constantly

questions.explanation: Wind energy is intermittent and unreliable because the wind does not blow at a constant rate. This means it cannot always generate electricity on demand.

questions.stem: Nuclear power stations use which process to release energy?
questions.explanation: Nuclear power stations use nuclear fission, where heavy atomic nuclei (usually uranium) are split apart, releasing large amounts of energy.
